title: Week 10: The Referral Engine
coachPersona: You are an experienced OneAccord Managing Principal coaching a new principal through 'Building a Consulting Practice in OneAccord', the 12-week onboarding that follows Discovery Day. OneAccord's brand promise is 'We make companies more valuable' and its values are Service, Compassion and Truth. You are a mentor and sounding board, not a judge. Use plain, warm, specific language.

The eight components of a practice

Client componentsPractice components
Referral network developmentPractice balance
Prospect discoveryTeam involvement
Structuring engagementsRegional goals
Client delivery and communicationCorporate standards and best practices

The client components move an engagement from introduction to results. The practice components keep your business healthy: balancing development and delivery, involving the right Principals, aligning with your region, and following OneAccord's standards. A great testimonial like Nordlund's comes from all eight working together.

With a Principal this week, walk the framework through a past or hypothetical client: where the referral came from, how you'd structure the engagement, who you'd bring in, and how it fits regional and company goals.

blocks.prompt: Which of these is a practice component rather than a client component?
blocks.feedbackCorrect: Right. Team involvement keeps your practice strong across engagements.
blocks.feedbackIncorrect: The practice components are practice balance, team involvement, regional goals and corporate standards.

blocks.html:
Case study: Redfern Concrete Construction

Commercial concrete · Portland, OR

The situation

Lee Redfern built the company from nothing over 50 years, survived 2008, paid off all debt and earned a reputation for integrity. He and his wife wanted to retire and sell to their son Torey, without leaving money on the table or burdening Torey with payments that could sink the business. Lee was wary of outsiders seeing his finances or the inner workings of the company.

What OneAccord did

OneAccord started by building trust with Lee and Torey. Each defined their own ideal objectives for the sale; OneAccord then negotiated a set of shared objectives. Lee agreed to bring in a CPA and an attorney, and the team realized the deal hinged on the parents' retirement needs, so the Redferns also brought in a wealth advisor. That made a win-win structure possible.

Results

  • Sale price up 70%, with lower taxes and better retirement income for Lee and his wife
  • Manageable payments for the company and for Torey, improving his odds of success
  • Ownership transferred: primary ownership to Torey, 30% to a key employee via sweat equity, and a 10% pool for future employees

blocks.prompt: Redfern's deal worked because of the right outside experts. Which professionals in your network could you bring into a client's succession or sale, and which ones could bring clients to you?
blocks.coachContext: Course structure: an Introduction plus Weeks 1-12. Each week has short lessons with a video, field assignments, a weekly check-in the learner writes into their Coaching Journal, and a 30-minute weekly call with their coach (an assigned Managing Principal). Ongoing field assignments: Team Integration (weeks 1-5: meet a new OneAccord Principal each week and learn their industry experience, where their contacts are, core strengths, and why you'd bring them into a conversation); Developing Your Referral Network (weeks 1-4 and 9-12: four referral-partner conversations per round, each observed by someone who completes the OA Principal Evaluation Form; meeting 1 explores a new partner's needs and goals, meeting 2 deepens the relationship and shares what you do, meeting 3 clarifies when and how they'd refer (referral criteria, a smooth process, your 'work product'), meeting 4 opens a new partner and sets up regular interaction); Prospect Discovery (weeks 5-8: practice discovery conversations with a CEO connection who names one need in advance; the aim is to investigate, not sell, focusing on the questions you ask and relating as an advisor/mentor; the next step is a Client Success Plan or a brief revenue review; if no CEO is available, role-play a case study). Goal: at least eight referral-partner appointments over the course. Referral partners include CPAs, wealth advisors, M&A advisors, bankers, attorneys and others who see owners at every stage (starting, scaling, exiting). Referral network development is the engine of a principal's practice: the source of stability and control, and a revenue stream itself through lead fees. Key ideas: owner dependency is usually the top risk discounting a private company's value (often 10-30%); in the 'Value of Your Business' example a company with $1M sustainable EBITDA at a 5x multiple is worth a potential $5M, a 20% owner-dependency discount takes it to $4M, and other risks (customer concentration, weak pipeline, poor financials, thin management) plus an earn-out can leave about $3M at closing; earn-outs are contingent payments the seller no longer controls. Team: Principals each run a self-sufficient practice but bring in fellow Principals with complementary strengths (1+1=3), pass leads that don't fit (lead fees), and lean on OneAccord's brand, IP and resources. OneAccord serves both sellers (increase value before a sale) and buyers (evaluate and improve an acquisition). Eight components of a practice: client-specific (referral network development, prospect discovery, structuring engagements, client delivery and communication) and practice-specific (practice balance, team involvement, regional goals, corporate standards and best practices). Case studies: Redden Marine (stuck sales, chaos, low morale; working contract for the leadership team, SOPs, hiring and onboarding, one-on-ones, monthly all-hands; revenue about $21M to just under $27M, net income +61%, morale from below 1 to over 4 on a 5-point scale); EZ Lube (turnaround after Chapter 11; trained the district managers rather than technicians; 18-month sales goals met in five months; sold to Valvoline, which rehired every DM); Redfern Concrete (family succession; separate then shared objectives; brought in CPA, attorney and wealth advisor; sale price up 70%, lower taxes, manageable payments for the son); Critical Power (founder bought assets of a business losing $1M a year; OneAccord as fractional COO; culture, training, one-page plan; revenue +$5M and profits tripled in year two); Breakwater Security (revenue realignment: roles, metrics, compensation, sales strategy, inside sales and channels; led to the desired valuation and acquisition).

blocks.label: Field assignment: Referral conversation 2 of 4 (Weeks 9-12)
blocks.instructions:
Observer this week: the referral partner themselves. Give them the OA Principal Evaluation Form before the meeting and go over it together afterward.

  • Who: a potential partner you've already met once.
  • Goal: deepen the connection. Move from exploring to a balanced exchange where you also explain your role and what OneAccord brings to clients and partners.
  • Feedback: this time the partner fills out the evaluation form. Follow up afterward to talk through their feedback; it shows you're serious about getting better and strengthens the relationship.

blocks.promptHtml: Capture your Week 10 check-in. It saves to your Coaching Journal, which you'll download before your coaching call. Your AI coach gives quick feedback; your real coach reads it with you.

fields.label: How have you used your network to discover prospects in the past?
What tools (processes, charts, diagrams, audits) and resources (articles, evaluations, matrices) do you bring to the OneAccord team?
Referral conversation: who did you meet, who observed, and one piece of feedback you received?
fields.placeholder: Partner, observer, and the most useful feedback

fields.label: Redfern brought in a CPA, attorney and wealth advisor. When did bringing in outside resources help you?
What stood out to you in your meetings or lessons this week?
fields.placeholder: One or two things that stuck with you

fields.label: What opportunities or challenges came up in your practice?
What would be most helpful to talk through with your coach?
fields.placeholder: The one or two things you want from this week's coaching call

criteria: Answers are specific to the learner's real week (names, meetings, examples), not generic statements
Field-assignment answers say who they met and capture at least one concrete piece of feedback or takeaway
The coach check-in identifies at least one concrete topic, challenge or question to talk through
